runs.title: Apply the Tribunal fix to payments/processor.ts

items.reason: `processCharge()` now reuses one promise per `order_id`, so two concurrent calls for the same order share the same charge instead of opening two separate network calls [payments/processor.ts:21-49]. That hides the double-charge path when `orders/checkout.ts` retries after the gateway times out at 2000ms, although a later retry after the first charge finishes can still start a new charge [gateway/proxy.ts:25-49][orders/checkout.ts:44-57].
items.reaction: `inFlightCharges` is a tiny bouncer for `ch_` IDs. The old code was a refund-shaped shitshow.

items.reason: The gateway configuration and timeout rules do not change, so it still forwards to `payments` at `http://localhost:4003` and still aborts after `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000` [gateway/config.ts:8-16][gateway/proxy.ts:25-49]. This change only makes `payments` less likely to process the same order twice while the first request is still running [payments/processor.ts:33-49].
items.reaction: `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` is still 2000ms. I did not get a damn new timeout.

items.reason: `checkout()` still calls `forward()` twice at most on `UpstreamTimeoutError`, and it still sends the same `order_id`, `amount`, `currency`, and `payment_method_id` shape to payments [orders/checkout.ts:20-30][orders/checkout.ts:44-57]. The new payment-side promise reuse only reduces duplicate work during an overlapping retry; it does not change the checkout code path here [payments/processor.ts:29-49].
items.reaction: `MAX_PAYMENT_ATTEMPTS` is still 2. The retry is ugly, but the charge duplication is less damn fragile now.

items.reason: `log()` is still called with the same events and fields from `processCharge()`: `charge processed` on success and `charge failed` on error [payments/processor.ts:38-49][payments/processor.ts:60-63]. This change only alters when `processCharge()` returns a shared result; it does not change the logger API or the shape of the log data.
items.reaction: `log('info', 'charge processed',...)` stays untouched; only the duplicate charge mess got quieter.

summary.update: Nothing else must change for this preview to work in the shown flow. If you want the fix to survive restarts or multiple `payments` instances, `payments/processor.ts` still needs a durable idempotency key instead of `inFlightCharges` in memory [payments/processor.ts:21-49].
summary.check: Run a concurrency test that fires two `processCharge()` calls with the same `order_id` before the first resolves and verify `network.authorizeAndCapture()` runs once and both callers get the same result. Also run the checkout timeout test to verify a retry after `UpstreamTimeoutError` no longer creates a second charge when the first request is still in flight [orders/checkout.ts:44-57][gateway/proxy.ts:25-49].

items.reason: Removing the second payment attempt means any timeout from `forward` now fails checkout immediately instead of being retried once. That makes transient slow responses from the payments service more visible, and a payment that takes longer than `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` 2000ms can still be reported as unavailable even if the charge may have gone through later [orders/checkout.ts:18-19][orders/checkout.ts:44-58][gateway/config.ts:15-16][gateway/proxy.ts:25-31][gateway/proxy.ts:45-49].
